paragraphs.title: Trust in God Amid the Threat of the Wicked

easy.explanation: The verse says, “In the LORD put I my trust.”
easy.q: In whom does the speaker say he has put his trust?

easy.explanation: The wicked bend their bow and make ready their arrow.
easy.q: What do the wicked prepare to shoot?

easy.explanation: The verse asks, “If the foundations be destroyed, what can the righteous do?”
easy.q: What is said to be destroyed in verse 3?

answers: To flee as a bird to his mountain
medium.explanation: The question, “How say ye to my soul, Flee as a bird to your mountain?” presents the advice to flee.
medium.q: What advice does the speaker reject?

medium.explanation: “Privily” means secretly, showing that the wicked intend to shoot without being noticed.
medium.q: In the phrase “privily shoot,” what does “privily” mean?

medium.explanation: The verse says they shoot “at the upright in heart.”
medium.q: Who are the wicked aiming at with their arrows?

answers: Trust in the LORD versus advice to flee
challenge.explanation: The speaker trusts in the LORD even while others urge him to escape.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in verses 1–3?

answers: They deliberately attack those who are righteous
They are unable to see their target
challenge.explanation: The phrase portrays the wicked as intentionally targeting people who are upright.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “shoot at the upright in heart” suggest about the wicked?

answers: What the righteous can do when the foundations of society collapse
How the righteous can build a larger bow
Where the righteous can find a mountain
challenge.explanation: The question considers the helplessness created when the foundations are destroyed.
challenge.q: What concern is expressed by the question, “What can the righteous do?”

answers: In his holy temple and on his throne in heaven
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD is in his holy temple” and that his throne is in heaven.
easy.q: Where is the LORD said to be?

easy.explanation: The verse specifically refers to “the children of men.”
easy.q: Whom do the LORD’s eyes behold and his eyelids try?

answers: Snares, fire and brimstone, and an horrible tempest
easy.explanation: These judgments are listed in verse 6 as the portion of the wicked’s cup.
easy.q: What will the LORD rain upon the wicked?

answers: A person who loves violent or harmful behavior
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies someone who loves violence, whom the LORD’s soul hates.
medium.q: What does “him that loveth violence” describe?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD trieth the righteous.”
medium.q: What does the LORD do to the righteous?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “For the righteous LORD loveth righteousness.”
medium.q: What does the LORD love according to verse 7?

answers: He tries the righteous but hates the wicked and those who love violence
He rewards the wicked and condemns the righteous
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the LORD’s testing of the righteous with his hatred and judgment of the wicked.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the LORD’s treatment of the righteous and the wicked?

answers: He observes and examines people before carrying out judgment
He judges without knowing what people do
He sees only the outward appearance of the righteous
challenge.explanation: The sequence emphasizes God’s complete awareness and examination before judgment.
challenge.q: What does the order of seeing, trying, and judging suggest about God?

answers: They shall receive the wicked’s weapons
They shall flee to a mountain
challenge.explanation: The final verse says, “his countenance doth behold the upright.”
challenge.q: What blessing is promised to the upright at the end of the passage?
